implementation: Host-only decode fairness and cohort-safe adaptive MTP policy
modifications: Reimplemented both policies as model-neutral host-only state machines; no peer scheduler or serving tree was copied.
Decode fairness derives a grid-aligned token cap from best observed prefill throughput, accrues bounded wall-time debt, and admits another chunk only after decode repays it.

Adaptive MTP aggregates acceptance across a whole physical cohort, applies one depth at a closed transaction boundary, supports depth-zero ordinary target parks, and guarantees bounded depth-one re-entry probes.
Only default-on bounded integer counters are retained; no device reads, synchronization, allocation, or hot-path timers are introduced by these policy objects.
validation: CPU policy, runtime, and serving tests cover wall-time cap/debt accounting, route-conditional fairness identity, contention reset, uniform physical-cohort depth changes, exact K=0 target parks, bounded K=1 re-entry, growth, admission-cap clamping, strict settings validation, qualification-only CLI selection, BatchGenerator propagation, profile identity, and receipt fields. On 2026-09-18, two concurrent live Qwen3.6-35B Apple-GPU requests observed adaptive_depth.selected=true, 81/98 boundaries, one depth change, current depth 1, and native-MTP acceptance 0.455/0.521. Decode fairness is selected only on ordinary/native-MTP BatchGenerator routes. The live run establishes mechanism engagement and finite output, not performance or quality qualification; adaptive MTP remains default-off and qualification-only.
